title: Institutional skepticism is redirecting trust toward familiar, local, and values-aligned actors
source_unit: Ipsos, Global Trends 10th Edition 2026: The Power of Trust, 21 September 2026
geography: Adults across 38 markets in the Ipsos Global Trends 2026 comparative framework

denominator.unit: markets in the Ipsos Global Trends comparative survey frame

government_distance.unit: percent saying their government does not prioritize their concerns

rigged_economy.unit: percent believing the economy is rigged in favor of the rich and powerful

legitimacy_route.value: institutional distance and perceived economic unfairness create demand for trust anchors closer to everyday life

observations.method: Ipsos Global Trends 2026 cross-market survey and published cultural-trend synthesis.
observations.uncertainty: The page reports cross-market aggregate findings without a single pooled population estimate; country differences, fieldwork, weighting, and question context matter.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, citizens, local communities, workers, people judging government responsiveness, and people experiencing economic inequality.
observations.counterinterpretation: Dissatisfaction with institutions can motivate reform and collective action rather than permanent withdrawal into private or local trust.

trust_shift.value: trust is becoming more personal, local, and values-driven rather than disappearing

familiarity.value: familiarity, localization, values, and purpose are identified as strong indicators for brand success amid institutional skepticism

social_route.value: local organizations and familiar relationships may function as legitimacy infrastructure when national institutions feel distant

observations.method: Ipsos macro-trend synthesis connecting trust, culture, institutions, and consumption across 38 markets.
observations.uncertainty: This is a framework for interpreting comparative signals, not a causal test showing that local trust produces stronger institutions, brands, or social cohesion.
observations.subgroup: Local communities, consumers, brands, civic organizations, public institutions, and groups with low confidence in national systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Local and familiar trust can be exclusionary, parochial, or vulnerable to misinformation; scale and impartiality may still require formal institutions.

observations.period: 2026; trust and consumption under AI change

consumer_translation.value: trust affects how people evaluate news, products, and services as institutional skepticism persists

ai_pressure.value: AI increases the need to understand how trust is generated and protected and how consumption patterns change

control_route.value: AI-mediated choice may intensify the premium on recognizable identity, values alignment, and accountable human or local intermediaries

observations.method: Ipsos published synthesis of trust, AI, news, products, and services; it is not an experiment or behavioral transaction dataset.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not establish whether local or values-aligned trust improves accuracy, welfare, purchasing outcomes, or AI safety.
observations.subgroup: AI users, news audiences, consumers, brands, local organizations, and people navigating automated recommendations.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI can also broaden access to information and comparison, weakening the role of familiar intermediaries rather than strengthening it.

open_test.value: test whether proximity, values alignment, and familiarity restore trust when formal institutions remain distrusted

measurement_chain.value: join perceived institutional responsiveness to local participation, consumer choice, information quality, public-service use, and durable collective action

boundary.value: trust redirection should not be treated as proof of institutional repair or a universal preference for local actors

observations.method: Program synthesis of the Ipsos publication with adjacent trust, media, consumer, and public-systems records.
observations.uncertainty: The proposed chain is a research direction, not a finding from the Ipsos page.
observations.subgroup: Citizens and consumers across countries, local institutions, national governments, brands, platforms, and civic intermediaries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal institutions may regain trust through visible performance, fairness, and accountability even when local relationships remain important.

related_sources.claim: The full Ipsos Global Trends 2026 publication provides the broader 38-market cultural and consumer framework.
Edelman provides a complementary cross-market account of insularity and institutional trust.

boundary: This record adds a distinct Ipsos publication route from institutional skepticism and perceived economic unfairness through local, familiar, values-aligned trust and AI-era consumption. It is aggregate comparative trend evidence, not respondent-level data, causal proof of local-trust effects, or a claim that formal institutions are becoming irrelevant.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Ipsos page was reviewed for the 38-market frame, government-prioritization share, economy-rigged share, trust transformation, consumer implications, AI context, and publication date.
